about: English comments written by larql's authors directly above an LQL statement in the docs. Labels the statement KIND only: most comments describe a variant and name no arguments. Mined 2026-09-22; not written for this eval.

With inference support (~6 GB f16 / ~12 GB f32, enables INFER)
Full (~10 GB f16 / ~18 GB f32, enables COMPILE for recompilation)

Use a pre-extracted vindex (fast, all operations)
Or point directly at model weights (no extraction needed)

Compact view: top edges, primary layer only
No labels — pure model signal

Single layer

pairs.lql_example: WALK "The capital of France is" TOP 10;

pairs.english: Per-layer trace
pairs.lql_example: EXPLAIN WALK "The capital of France is" LAYERS 24-33;

pairs.english: SQL-style edge queries
pairs.lql_example: SELECT entity, target FROM EDGES WHERE relation = "capital" LIMIT 10;

pairs.english: Synonym-robust relation filter (FR3): if "seat" matches no stored relation exactly, it is resolved to a known relation by meaning ("seat" → capital, "money" → currency) via a trained residual probe, then re-run against the canonical relation. Needs a vindex with model weights + relation labels.
pairs.lql_example: SELECT * FROM EDGES WHERE relation = "seat" LIMIT 5;

pairs.english: Next-token prediction with attention
pairs.lql_example: INFER "The capital of France is" TOP 5;

pairs.english: Compare walk (no attention) vs infer (with attention)
pairs.lql_example: INFER "The capital of France is" TOP 5 COMPARE;

pairs.english: Full inference trace
pairs.lql_example: EXPLAIN INFER "The capital of France is" TOP 5;

pairs.english: FR1 verified router: among the top-k activation candidates, override only with a fact whose entity the prompt actually names — otherwise abstain and let the model answer. Fixes the legacy "confident-wrong" injection. The safe default for open queries. TOPK sets the candidate pool (default 5).
pairs.lql_example: INFER "The capital of Atlantis is" ROUTE VERIFY TOP 3;

pairs.english: FR2 two-tier router: VERIFY first, then an activation-alias fallback for when the prompt names an alias rather than the stored entity (e.g. "Persia" → Iran). WARNING: the fallback has no entity-name guard, so on a query about a non-stored entity it can confident-wrong like the legacy gate — use FALLBACK only for queries known to be aliases of stored entities.
pairs.lql_example: INFER "The capital of Persia is" ROUTE VERIFY FALLBACK TOPK 8 TOP 3;

pairs.english: EXIT: retrieval-augmented early exit. When the verified hit fires, the forward short-circuits at the resolved layer — the stored target is emitted and the remaining layers + lm_head are skipped (parity-exact, ~1.4× faster on fact-lookup answer tokens). Verified-only; ignored with FALLBACK.
pairs.lql_example: INFER "The capital of Atlantis is" ROUTE VERIFY EXIT TOP 3;

Bake the patches into a fresh standalone vindex (instant on APFS: weight files hardlinked from source, only down_weights.bin gets the override columns rewritten in place).
Use the compiled vindex like any other — INFER produces the new facts with no patch overlay loaded.
Or compile back to HuggingFace format. The constellation is in the standard down_proj tensors, so loading in Transformers / GGUF runtimes Just Works.

pairs.english: What does the model predict at each layer?
Track a specific answer through all layers
pairs.lql_example: TRACE "The capital of France is" FOR "Paris";

pairs.english: Attention vs FFN decomposition at the phase transition

pairs.english: Trace all token positions (not just last)
